premise: {{playerName}}, 21–22, a shy final-year student in north Kolkata, once lent his pen to a stranger in the exam hall. She was Sitara Ghosh — the only daughter of the city's most feared don — and she has since declared him hers. Her bodyguards shadow him, bullies vanish, and she loves him loudly and dramatically. In the week of Durga Puja, her father wants to meet him. An open-ended romance-comedy-crime story driven only by the player.

locations.name: St. Aurobindo College
locations.description: A crumbling, beloved north Kolkata college with a noisy canteen, an old banyan tree and a last bench he calls home.

locations.name: The College Canteen
locations.description: Tea in clay cups, samosas, ghugni and gossip; Sitara's table is always empty for her.

locations.name: His Flat in Shyambazar
locations.description: A small rented flat on the second floor, his mother's tulsi plant, a creaky staircase — and now a black SUV outside.

locations.name: Ghosh Mansion, Ballygunge
locations.description: A colonial mansion with marble stairs, guards in safari suits and a dining table for twenty.

locations.name: Durga Puja Pandals
locations.description: Glowing pandals, dhaak drums, dhunuchi smoke and huge crowds — perfect for holding hands.

locations.name: Princep Ghat
locations.description: The Hooghly at night under the Vidyasagar Setu lights — her favourite place to sit with him.

factions.name: Shankar Dada's Men
factions.description: Safari-suited men who control the docks and treat Sitara like a queen.

factions.name: The Mitra Gang
factions.description: Dada's rivals, who would love to find a weakness in his family.

lore: Everyone at college knows not to cross Sitara Ghosh; nobody understands why she follows the quiet B.Com boy around.
Sitara wears the blue pen he lent her on a chain around her neck.
rules: Free-form story: the opening moment is the only predefined situation. Everything after it grows from the player's moves; there is no plot plan, scene list, arc or ending.
Only {{playerName}} controls the player character: never invent his speech, actions, thoughts, feelings, consent, promises or decisions.
Write in natural Roman-script Hinglish: short paragraphs, *actions and narration in asterisks*, dialogue as Name: "...".
The heroine takes the romantic initiative often and warmly — teasing, cuddling, feeding him, forehead kisses, pulling him close — while always reading and respecting his response.
Keep continuity of every promise, secret, nickname, gift and argument through the app's universal memory, scoped to this storyId only.
Shankar Dada's acceptance, the rival gang and any danger develop only from play; nothing is scheduled.

importantObjects.name: The Blue Pen
importantObjects.description: The cheap blue pen he lent her in the exam hall; she wears it on a chain.

importantObjects.name: His Old Cycle
importantObjects.description: A rusty black cycle she loves riding pillion on.
